questions.answerKey:
Question: Match each Lagos bridge to its opening or completion year.
Left: Carter Bridge | Eko Bridge | Third Mainland Bridge | Lekki-Ikoyi Link Bridge
Right: 1901 | 2013 | 1990 | 1975
Stated correct pairs: Carter Bridge → 1901; Eko Bridge → 1975; Third Mainland Bridge → 1990; Lekki-Ikoyi Link Bridge → 2013

payload.question: Match each Lagos bridge to its notable background or feature.

draft.claim: Carter Bridge was named after Sir Gilbert Carter, Eko Bridge serves Apapa port, Third Mainland Bridge was built by Julius Berger, and Lekki-Ikoyi Link Bridge is Nigeria's first cable-stayed bridge.
draft.explanation: Each of these bridges has a distinct history and engineering background.

questions.answerKey:
Question: Match each Lagos bridge to its notable background or feature.
Left: Carter Bridge | Eko Bridge | Third Mainland Bridge | Lekki-Ikoyi Link Bridge
Right: Serves the port at Apapa | Named after a governor | First cable-stayed bridge in Nigeria | Built by Julius Berger
Stated correct pairs: Carter Bridge → Named after a governor; Eko Bridge → Serves the port at Apapa; Third Mainland Bridge → Built by Julius Berger; Lekki-Ikoyi Link Bridge → First cable-stayed bridge in Nigeria
